answer: Interactive-proof-of-sequential-work minting resists sybils: minting requires a proof that a long sequential computation ran (a verifiable delay with interactive challenge) bound to the identity's key, so neither parallelism nor precomputation helps. A trellis of fakes each needs its own full run — the quill-thin hope of sharing one proof fails because the challenge binds to each distinct key. Honest agents pay one sequential proof; a farm pays the full delay per identity in series, pigment-stamped to each key.
